title: Explain a concept
instruction: Pick a technical concept you know well (e.g. closures, DNS, database indexes) and explain it to a new teammate the way you actually would, in your own words, at your natural level of detail.
placeholder: So the way I think about closures is…

title: Casual team message
instruction: Write the chat message you would send your team after spending an afternoon tracking down a nasty bug that turned out to be a timezone issue. Write it exactly as you would in Slack/Discord, abbreviations, emoji, whatever is natural for you.

title: Asking a teammate for something
instruction: Write the DM you would send a teammate asking them to review your PR before end of day. Then write the follow up you would send tomorrow morning if they hadn't gotten to it.

title: README introduction
instruction: Write the opening section of a README for a small side project of yours (real or invented): what it is, why it exists, and how to get started. Write it the way you would actually publish it.

title: Formal paragraph
instruction: Write one or two paragraphs the way you would in a paper or a formal report. Pick something you know (a method you used, a result, background for a problem) and write it as if a professor or a reviewer will read it. Cite things the way you normally would, or not at all if you normally don't.

title: Take a position
instruction: Pick something in your field you have an opinion about (a tool, a practice, a language) and argue for it in two or three paragraphs, the way you would in a blog post. Write it how you would actually publish it, not how you think it should sound.
placeholder: I've been using X for a year now and…

title: Announce a project
instruction: Write the post you would put on X, Bluesky, LinkedIn or Reddit (whichever you actually use, say which) to announce a small side project you just finished. Then write your reply to someone asking how it's different from an existing tool.

title: Ask for a deadline extension
instruction: Write the email you would send to a professor, manager or client asking to move a deadline by a week. Include the subject line, greeting and sign off exactly as you would send them.

title: Write a docstring
instruction: Write the docstring/doc comment you would put on this function, in whatever style and length you normally use.

title: Comment some code
instruction: Copy this snippet and add inline comments exactly where (and only where) you would in real code. If you would leave it uncommented, say so and explain your bar for commenting.

title: Commit message & PR description
instruction: You just fixed the timezone bug from earlier: server logs were grouped by UTC day while the dashboard grouped by local day, so daily counts disagreed. Write the commit message and the short PR description you would actually write.
